summary: Six semantic proof operations. Contract requirements, controlled-acceptance applicability, obligation meaning and shared cases are authored and read through ordinary obligation coverage operations, then explicitly validated or verified.

tools.notes: Find proof candidates by the property to establish: a query returns bounded ranked pages of compact rows (identity, intent ids, match kind, query-relevant limitation, verification capability, detail_action) and adds no unmatched proof; no query browses the catalogue compactly. Source-bound continuation reaches every match. Selected detail returns a candidate's complete assertion, exclusions and comparisons, with field/range continuation. Provider terms stay context, not relevance. Query maximum: 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Read-only; does not select or execute proofs.
use_when: Find ranked proof candidates for an obligation's property, browse the catalogue compactly, or read the complete scope of a known proof name.
do_not_use_when: Select or map proofs, supply instance inputs, construct or execute a proof.
authoritative_for: lexical candidate discovery and exact admitted proof scope

recommended_first_call.operation: query by the property to establish, then read the selected candidate's detail; use proof_name for known exact detail

use_when: An authenticated orchestrator must verify the complete proof population selected by one canonical WK, slice, test-proof, or obligation subject against the configured clean or dirty worktree, or against a shared authenticated private detached materialization of an exact full Git commit.

Read the selected test observation and mutation evidence separately: mutation contributes additional falsification evidence for the same proof, while unavailable mutation leaves the observed test result visible and unchanged.

A test-proof or obligation ID is saved in more than one source: the bare call refuses and lists every authorized source choice; retry one listed choice, which adds source {unit, focus?} to select exactly that WK or slice source (omitted focus selects the root source) without searching any other source.
An eligible launcher-managed worker or reviewer must execute every exact server-resolved declared test proof selected by one canonical subject.

A proof definition (declarative test selector, boundary, observable, falsifiers, traversal) has been authored and the candidate implementation must now be executed against it; a selected test that does not exist yet is an execution outcome of this call, never an authoring prerequisite.

Each selected test runs in the setup-prepared environment its saved runner binding and owning installation root select (the target suffix is recorded as a hint), so one call may verify several languages; pass optional environment <ecosystem>@<installation root> (for example npm@. or go_modules@services/api, as setup's readiness lists them) to name one prepared environment, which must serve every selected proof or the call refuses before executing and lists each incompatible target with the valid choices.
do_not_use_when: A managed worker or reviewer wants to supply git_sha or escape its launcher-bound candidate.
The subject is a WK ID or slice address and a source is also supplied; a population subject already names its source, and source never grants execution or declaration authority.

The task needs a caller-selected path, command, target, environment variables, executable, root or mount, provider, evaluator, receipt, policy, authority, arbitrary test execution, replay authority, or lifecycle authority; environment names only a setup-published prepared environment.
authoritative_for: advisory satisfied, unsatisfied, not_executable, or typed-refusal verification of one deterministic, completely preflighted proof population, including separate selected-test observations and additional mutation falsification evidence, with canonical relationship projection, authenticated selected-worktree facts, confined execution, receipt, proof-pack, and evaluator identities

recommended_first_call.operation: verify one canonically selected proof population

tools.display_name: Save or amend proof obligations and shared cases
use_when: Save one or many obligations, proof selections and unfinished shared cases; reference, complete or correct them later using case_id.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.

recommended_first_call.operation: Save or amend a proof obligation

tools.notes: List-only atomic amendment. Omitted fields preserve values; clear_parameters removes named explicit parameters. case supplies component, target/selector, observation and falsification meaning. One case definition lives in the parent obligation source; obligations and slices reference case_id. Missing fields stay absent. Native structures are derived. All affected uses are checked before effects. CAS binds the source closure, canonical facts and target state. Normal receipt is exactly {unit,saved,unchanged,content_digest}; query returns saved semantic cases. A test_execution verification saves its specific meaning -- verifier, observation and falsifying condition -- without verification.runtime_test; supplying runtime_test additionally binds the executable test. An authored case, a native provider selector, an installed executor and a supported falsifier target are execution inputs, never conditions of saving or admitting the plan. No execution or separate preparation route is required.

tools.display_name: Remove a proof selection or obligation
use_when: Remove only a saved proof selection so the obligation can be selected again, or explicitly remove the complete obligation row.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.

recommended_first_call.operation: Remove a proof selection or obligation row

tools.notes: removal_scope is mandatory under the current contract. selection clears only the case use, proof selection, pins and parameters while retaining obligation meaning for reselection. obligation deletes the complete row while retaining contract requirements, shared cases and sibling parent/slice uses. Neither mode rewrites historical evidence, grants proof credit or authorizes dispatch. Repeating selection removal is a CAS-checked no-op; repeating obligation removal returns obligation_not_found.

use_when: Read saved obligations and complete requirement meaning after restart, optionally selecting one obligation or pinned parameter detail, or listing obligation IDs with their statements when they are unknown.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.
tools.notes: Read saved obligations, exact pins, incomplete linked cases and complete requirement meaning after restart. Selectors resolve against deduplicated canonical references in the response. obligation_id limits requirements and references to associated meaning; counts disclose omissions. inventory answers the unknown-ID case with one compact row per obligation -- authored statement plus factual gap, selection and case indicators -- a contract-input summary and ONE shared detail-read declaration, and is refused alongside obligation_id or parameter_detail; read the whole population unselected instead of walking an inventory row by row. Combined revision is the next CAS. Paging requires no validation or construction.

use_when: Explicitly check saved proof inputs against the exact selected route and distinguish blocking, nonblocking and unresolved author-input, canonical-source or system-capability diagnostics without execution or mutation.

Inspect the authored-semantic verdict separately from selected-route executable-map stages, zero-credit execution status, dispatch-not-assessed status, and supported or explicitly unavailable recovery.
Retrieve every original occurrence for a returned diagnostic_group_id through the same source-bound validation route.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.
tools.notes: Explicit design validation of saved obligations, exact pins and pack-owned parameters/construction/dependencies. Root status, input_status and valid/invalid obligation counts report existing authored meaning and currentness; rows without a selected route remain in that denominator. The strict executable-map verdict, exact route stages and route-effect counts stay under selected_route_assessment. diagnostic_group_id selects lossless identity-bound detail. Every resolved-unit response offers workspace_validate_dispatch as an independent assessment regardless of executable-map validity; validation does not invoke it, grant dispatch, execute proofs, mutate authored state or grant readiness authority.
